text: Consider the orthonormal set of vectors $$ \uvec_1=\threevec{1/\sqrt{3}}{-1/\sqrt{3}}{1/\sqrt{3}}, \hspace{24pt} \uvec_2=\threevec{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/\sqrt{2}}0 $$ and the matrix they define $$ Q = \begin{bmatrix} 1/\sqrt{3} \amp 1/\sqrt{2} \\ -1/\sqrt{3} \amp 1/\sqrt{2} \\ 1/\sqrt{3} \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}\text{.} $$ In this case, $\uvec_1$ and $\uvec_2$ span a plane, a 2-dimensional subspace of $\real^3$. We know that $Q^TQ = I_2$ and $QQ^T$ projects vectors orthogonally onto the plane. However, $Q$ is not a square matrix so it cannot be invertible.
